How water stressed is {% if (data['watertype'] == "ground")%}{{data.groundwaterCatchmentData[data.gid].properties.WB_NAME}}{% elseif (data['watertype'] == "surface")%}{{data.riverCatchmentData[data.sid].properties.WB_NAME}}{% endif %}

Some areas are more water stressed than others. We class water bodies as 'low', 'moderate' or 'highly stressed'.

How water stressed your local area is depends on how much water is already licenced and whether areas nearby need protection.

In highly stressed areas there is less water available for abstraction, especially in times of drought, In these areas there are strict restrictions on how much water you can take and when you are allowed to abstract. You can learn more below.

Understanding groundwater availability

Water availability will depend on the location and depth of abstraction.

A pump test or hydrogeological impact assessment will be needed to determine licence availability for your specific abstraction point. You must contact the Environment Agency (see details below) to find out whether you need to get consent to investigate the groundwater source or prepare a hydrogeological impact assessment before you can apply for a licence.

Regulations and restrictions

Restrictions may apply to licences where availability is limited or to protect the environment.

Hands-off Flow and Hands-off Levels are set by the Environment Agency as conditions on licences, these prevent abstractors from taking water when levels drop below a certain point.

Get advice on groundwater availability and licensing

Contact the Environment Agency for more information on groundwater availability and licensing.
